rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders balanced spending through the image of neither tying one's hand to one's neck nor opening it completely, which leaves one regretful and exposed.
rows.anchor: Hem elini bağlayıp boynuna asma hem de onu büsbütün açıp saçma ki pişman olur, açık kalırsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom of striking their ears means laying the youths down and putting them to sleep.
rows.anchor: kulakları üzerine vurduk yani yatırdık uyuttuk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's saying that He might know means bringing the matter to manifestation and making it clear, so that the youths themselves understand.
rows.anchor: burada “bilelim” demek fiilen tebeyyün, tahakkuk ettirelim de kendileri dahi anlasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties are the monotheist believing Companions of the Cave and their polytheist opponents.
rows.anchor: iki hizibden birisi muvahhid, mü’min olan Ashâb-ı Kehf, birisi de hasımları olan müşriklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On waking, the youths saw that they had succeeded in their undertaking and goals and had attained divine mercy.
rows.anchor: uyandıkları zaman işlerinde muvaffak olduklarını, gayelerinde isabet ettiklerini gördüler ve rahmet-i ilâhiyeye kavuştular

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitya is the plural of fetā, meaning a young man, lad, or brave youth, and is a plural of paucity.
rows.anchor: genç, delikanlı, yiğit demek olan “fetâ”nın cem‘-i kılletidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names, exact number, and homeland are not needed for the exemplary truth of the story; their defining traits matter.
rows.anchor: Demek ki kıssanın ibret teşkil eden hakikatinde bunların isimleri ve adedleri ve memleketleri bellenmek lâzım değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths believed in their Lord, and God increased their guidance.
rows.anchor: kendilerinin Rabbine iman ettiler ve kendilerine hidâyeti müzdâd kıldık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened their hearts, giving them firmness and resolve.
rows.anchor: ve kalblerine râbıta verdik metânetleştirdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their defining act was to rise against polytheists and publicly proclaim God's oneness.
rows.anchor: İşte bu yiğitlerin işlerinin esası bu idi. Müşriklere karşı kıyam ile i‘lân-ı tevhid

rows.speaker: Muhammed b. İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account describes Christian turmoil and tyrannical kings, especially Decianus, who persecuted Christians refusing pagan worship.
rows.anchor: Muhammed b. İshak’ın nakline göre şöyle zikredilmiştir: Ehl-i İncil’in işi herc ü merc oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were free young men of Roman nobility; one report says they belonged to the king's inner circle.
rows.anchor: Rum’un zâdegânından ve bir kavle göre melikin havâssından hür gençlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the emperor offered worship of idols or death, the youths rejected the invitation and professed faith in their one Lord.
rows.anchor: bunları ya putlara ibadet veya ölüm ile tahyir etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being dismissed with time to reconsider, they resolved to protect their faith by fleeing to a steep cave on Mount Benclus near the city.
rows.anchor: şehrin yakınındaki Benclüs dağında sarp bir mağaraya gizlenmeye karar verdiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They entrusted Yemliha with provisions; he entered town disguised as a poor man, bought what was needed, and returned with news.
rows.anchor: O sabahleyin bir miskin kıyafetine girerek şehre giriyor, lâzım olanı alıyor, biraz da havâdis tecessüs edip arkadaşlarına dönüyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the emperor returned, the youths prayed and fell asleep; God moved him to wall up the cave as their tomb.
rows.anchor: Dekyanus mağaranın kapısının ördürülmesini emretti. “Açlıktan susuzluktan ölsünler, mağaraları kabirleri olsun” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two believers in the emperor's household, Pendros and Runas, concealed the youths' names, lineage, and story on lead tablets in a copper case inside the wall.
rows.anchor: birinin adı Pendros öbürününki Runas idi. Bunlar Ashâb-ı Kehf’in isimlerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were true believers who preserved their faith against coercive polytheist rulers by God's guidance and protection.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı bu yiğitler Allah’tan başka ilâh tanımaz, hakikaten mü’min idiler, işleri de Allah’ın hidâyet ve ismetiyle dinlerini muhafaza için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Christians who deified the Messiah and pursued worldly adornment, the youths stood together in firm monotheism.
rows.anchor: Şirke sapan ve Mesih’e rab, ilâh diyen, dünya ziynet ve hayâtına rağbet eyleyen Nasârâya benzemiyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call any deity besides God impossible and false, so claiming another god is irrational and a lie.
rows.anchor: çünkü ondan başka ilâh muhaldir, yalandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge that their people took gods besides God includes idol worship, polytheism generally, and those who call the Messiah divine.
rows.anchor: putlara boyun eğenler ve ale’l-umûm müşrikler bu tâbirde dâhil olduğu gibi, “Mesih ilâhtır” diyenler dahi dâhil olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth are clear proofs of God's divinity; challengers have no proof for another deity, and arbitrary power is no evidence.
rows.anchor: Delilsiz dava kabul edilir mi? Veya şunun bunun keyfî tahakkümü, tasallutu delil tutulur mu?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı also allows the reading that the people fail to produce effective verbal or practical evidence against the youths' proof, yet persist in falsehood.
rows.anchor: Burada şu mâna da muhtemildir: Onlar aleyhine bizim yaptığımız gibi ilmî amelî, kavlî fiilî müessir bir beyyine getirmiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing charge echoes the earlier statement that they utter only lies and also serves as evidence against those who claim God has a son.
rows.anchor: yukarıda geçen إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًا fâsılasına lafzen ve mânen terdif ve ircâ‘ı açıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story's judgment against polytheists also proves against those who say God has taken a son.
rows.anchor: aynı zamanda bunun ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًا diyenler aleyhine hükmü ihtivâ eden bir delil olduğu da anlatılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths expect their retreat to bring God's mercy and ease; the light of faith ultimately leads to the mercy of the All-Merciful and success in their aim.
rows.anchor: zira nûr-i imanın âkıbet rahmet-i Rahmân’a kavuşturacağı muhakkaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer to receive mercy and right guidance was followed by God putting them to sleep, either to shield them from oppressors' distress or after the cave entrance was walled.
rows.anchor: kulaklarının üzerine vurulup yani o zâlimler tarafından bir keder işitilmemek için yatırılıp veyahut mağaranın kapısına bir binâ kurdurulup senelerce uyutuldular

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave is protected on every side; its entrance faces north with a slight western inclination, so direct sunlight scarcely reaches them.
rows.anchor: mağaranın vaziyeti budur. Her tarafı mahfuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths lie comfortably in a spacious area inside the cave.
rows.anchor: bir geniş yerinde sıkıntısız yatıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stand for God, reliance on Him, and protected position in the cave are signs of divine power and mercy and a karama.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın âyetlerinden ilâhî alâmetlerden, kudret ve rahmet-i ilâhiye burhanlarından biridir, bir keramettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided are truly on the right path, as the Cave companions were; those God leaves astray find no guiding patron and remain lost despite such signs.
rows.anchor: Allah her kime hidâyet ederse doğru yolu tutan odur. Nitekim Ashâb-ı Kehf böyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although asleep, the companions' eyes were open, making them look awake.
rows.anchor: Demek ki uykuda oldukları hâlde gözleri açık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned them from side to side, while their dog lay at the cave entrance with its forelegs outstretched; their fearful appearance made discovery impossible.
rows.anchor: Köpekleri de kollarını sermiş ağızda mağaranın medhalinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who saw them would flee, filled with terror; their awe prevented anyone from learning their condition.
rows.anchor: ve mutlak korkudan dolardın vaziyetleri öyle heybetli, öyle korkunç idi. Demek ki kendilerine kimsenin ittilâ‘ı kābil değildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their awakening, like a sign of resurrection, first served to let them understand their own condition; knowing one's state is among the foremost concerns.
rows.anchor: ilm-i hâl akdem-i umûr olduğundan ba‘slerinin ilk hikmeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some estimated one day and others part of a day; people raised at resurrection will likewise make such an estimate, as in the passage about the passerby in 2:259.
rows.anchor: Nitekim kıyamette ba‘s olunacaklar hep böyle sanacaklar (Sûre-i Bakara’da أَوْ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ ilh. [2/259] bak)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When some sensed they had slept longer, they ended the disagreement by acknowledging that their Lord knew the duration.
rows.anchor: Rabbiniz a‘lemdir. Binâen‘aleyh ihtilâfı bırakınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sent one companion with their silver coin to find the cleanest food and bring provisions, acting carefully and keeping their presence secret.
rows.anchor: ve size ondan bir rızık getirsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If discovered, they feared being stoned or forced back into their former religion; death as martyrs would be escape, but apostasy would bring eternal loss because worldly life ends and disbelief's afterlife punishment is eternal.
rows.anchor: Zira hayât-ı dünya fânîdir, herkese ölüm muhakkaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text raises whether coercion excuses outward apostasy while faith remains inwardly firm, citing the exception in 16:106.
rows.anchor: kalblerindeki imanı bozmadan ikrah ile zâhiren dönmüş olsalardı إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُۥ مُطْمَئِنٌّۢ بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ [en-Nahl 16/106] istisnâsına dâhil olmazlar mıydı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, they are men of resolve whose success means spreading mercy inwardly and outwardly, not merely escaping liability; for them acting on a dispensation is less than perfect.
rows.anchor: Bunlar azimet ricâli yiğitlerdir. Gözettikleri felâh yalnız mes’ûliyetten halâs değil, zâhiren ve bâtınen neşr-i rahmettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, they spoke before actual coercion to avoid falling into it; negligence that leads to coercion does not remove responsibility.
rows.anchor: Bu söz henüz ikrah hâlinde değil, ikrah vaziyetine düşmekten son derece ihtiraz için söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, prolonged coercion that habituates one to disbelief and shakes settled faith risks the warning that obeying them makes one a polytheist.
rows.anchor: küfre itiyad gibi herhangi bir sebeble kalbin imana itmi’nânını sarsacak surette devam edeceği muhakkak olan ikrahlara muvâfakatin de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported account says the sent companion's coin led to his discovery and thereby brought the people to learn about the sleepers.
rows.anchor: gidenin elindeki para yakalanmasına sebep olmuş ve bu yüzden Allah teâlâ üzerlerine halkı muttali‘kılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleepers themselves recognized that God's promise was true and the Hour certain when they awoke as if from graves, saw their success against the persecutors, and witnessed the mercy they had hoped for.
rows.anchor: vaktiyle kıyam ettikleri müşriklere karşı muvaffak olduklarını ve taleb ü ümid ettikleri merhamet-i ilâhiyenin bir tecellîsini görmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their story became a proof and example for themselves and others that resurrection is certain.
rows.anchor: kıyametin şüphesiz olduğuna da bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people disputed what to do with the cave companions and proposed building over them so the cave could serve as their tomb.
rows.anchor: da “üzerlerine bir binâ yapın” demişlerdi mağarayı kabirleri olsun diye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prevailed are identified as the party that followed the companions' cause and achieved victory over their enemies; they proposed a mosque over them.
rows.anchor: Ashâb-ı Kehf’in tâkip ettiği emir üzerine giderek düşmanlarına karşı galebeye nâil olmuş olan hizb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people speculate about the unseen, so Elmalılı advises limiting discussion to a superficial debate rather than prolonged disputation.
rows.anchor: bilenler azdır, çoğu gayb taşlıyorlar. Onun için zâhirî bir münakaşadan başka bir mücadele ve mübahaseye dalma

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing the companions' exact number is unnecessary to the lesson, and only a few know it; most people speculate about the unseen.
rows.anchor: Adedlerinin bilinmesi kıssa nokta-i nazarından herkese lâzım değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should avoid prolonged argument about the sleepers and should not ask any of the competing claimants; the Quran already explains what needs to be known.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde Ashâb-ı Kehf kıssasını yalnız Kur’ân’ın beyânına dikkat ederek okumalı, şundan bundan sormaya kalkışmamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human resolve alone cannot bring an event about, so plans for the future must be tied to God's will; a person does not know what tomorrow will bring.
rows.anchor: insanın azm ü iradesi bir şeyin husûlü için sebeb-i kâfî değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one forgets to say “if God wills,” one should remember God when recalling it, by saying it then or by glorification and seeking forgiveness; this expiates the lapse even if it does not change the statement's effect.
rows.anchor: unuttuğun vakit de Rabbini an yani bu istisnâyı hasbe’lbeşeriyye unutmuş bulunursan hatırladığın zaman “inşaallah” diyerek veya tesbih ve istiğfar ederek Allah’ı zikret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading is that remembering God after forgetting anything acknowledges human weakness and may help one recall the forgotten thing.
rows.anchor: Veya herhangi bir şeyi unuttuğun zaman acz-i beşerîyi düşünüp Allah’ı yâd et ki unuttuğunu hatırlayabilesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignoring God's will when promising what one will certainly do tomorrow is blameworthy; even the possibility of forgetting and speaking falsely is enough to see the problem.
rows.anchor: “yarın muhakkak şöyle yapacağım, böyle yapacağım” demenin mahzurlarını anlamak için bir insan lâ-ekal unutup yalan çıkacağını düşünmek bile kifayet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks that the Lord bring the Prophet to success more directly than the Cave companions' success.
rows.anchor: bundan (yani Ashâb-ı Kehf’in muvaffakiyetinden) daha çok yakın bir suretle beni muvaffakiyete eriştirmesi pek me’muldür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three hundred years plus nine gives the lunar equivalent of three hundred solar years.
rows.anchor: sene-i şemsiye üç yüz, dokuz fazlası da sene-i kameriye hesâbıyladır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators hold that the duration is God's own statement.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn bu müddetin beyân-ı ilâhî olduğuna kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ud
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud takes the duration as a quotation of those disputing the count, with an omitted “they said.”
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ud’dan mervî olduğu üzere وقالوا takdîriyle adedde ihtilâf edenlerin sözünü hikâye olduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators prefer connecting the duration to the statement of those who said they would build a mosque over the sleepers.
rows.anchor: diğer bazıları da tâ yukarıda قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِمْ’deki وَقُلْ’nin mekūlüne ma‘tuf olarak “mescid yapalım” diyenlerin sözü olmasını tercih etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers a fresh, resumptive reading: the victorious Cave party remained hidden in their cave for 309 years, until their side prevailed.
rows.anchor: Ashâb-ı Kehf’in hizbi demek olan ve “mescid yapalım” diyen ٱلَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا۟’ya râci‘olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects their emergence with Christians overcoming the idolatrous Romans at the beginning of the fourth century, which fits a hiding period of more than three hundred years.
rows.anchor: Nasârânın müşrik Romalılara galebe ile meydana çıkmaları Milâdın dördüncü asrı bidâyetlerinde vâki‘olduğuna göre o zamana kadar üç yüz küsur sene durmuşlar demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their long hidden victory foreshadows that Muhammad's mission and Islam would prevail sooner and more swiftly and beautifully, a triumph that began after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: üç yüz dokuz sene gizli durdukları hâlde risâlet-i Muhammediye ile dîn-i İslâm’ın bundan çok az bir müddet zarfında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people dispute how long they stayed, answer that God knows best, as the sleepers themselves said; He owns heaven and earth's unseen and sees and hears perfectly.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Ashâb-ı Kehf kendileri de رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثْتُمْ demişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions have no patron apart from God and are not among those who claim He has a son; no one shares in God's judgment.
rows.anchor: Yani Ashâb-ı Kehf ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًا diyenlerden değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders God's revealed words as unchangeable and says no refuge can be found apart from Him.
rows.anchor: O’nun kelimâtını tebdil edecek yoktur ve O’ndan başka bir penâh bulamazsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who pray morning and evening are rendered as seeking their Lord's beauty; the Prophet is told not to turn his eyes away from them for worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: Rablerine dua eder, cemâlini isterler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The torment passage is rendered as scalding water that chars faces and a wretched drink and “kurultay” (gathering place).
rows.anchor: o ne fena içki ve o ne fena kurultay

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's owner is told he should have said “What God wills; there is no strength except through God” when entering it.
rows.anchor: Bağına girdiğin vakit مَا شَٓاءَ اللهُّٰۙ لاَ قُوَّةَ اِلاَّ بِاللهِّٰ dese idin olmaz mıydı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his wealth was overtaken and the garden collapsed over its trellises, the man wrung his hands over his expenses and wished he had not associated anyone with God.
rows.anchor: bütün serveti istîlâ ediliverdi, bunun üzerine ona yaptığı masraflara karşı avuçlarını oğuşturdu kaldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is likened to rain that mixes with the earth's plants, then becomes scraps scattered by winds; God has power over everything.
rows.anchor: derken bir çöp kırıntısı olmuştur, rüzgârlar onu savurur gider. Allah her şeye muktedir bulunuyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls them the greatest losers in deeds: their worldly striving comes to nothing while they imagine they are doing excellent work.
rows.anchor: Onlar ki dünyâ hayatta saʿyleri boşa gitmektedir de kendilerini zannederler ki cidden güzel sanat yapıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rendering says the Merciful will create affection for believers who do righteous deeds and make them loved in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: Rahmân onlar için bir meveddet (bir sevgi) verecek, gönüllere sevdirecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports the revelation occasion as follows: As b. Wa'il owed Khabbab, demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad, then promised to repay him after resurrection when he expected wealth and children.
rows.anchor: Âs b. Vâil sebebiyle nâzil olmuştu, şöyle ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lizām means punishment that immediately clings in this world, as happened to 'Ad and Thamud.
rows.anchor: “Lizâm” Âd ve Semûd’a olduğu gibi hemen dünyada yapışan azab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer instructions here set out all of the prayer times.
rows.anchor: Burada da namaz vakitleri tamamıyla gösterilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran answers the demand for a sign by clearly explaining and proving the contents of the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books, making Muhammad's prophethood manifest.
rows.anchor: Tevrat ve İncil vesâir semâvî kitapların mündericâtını daha açık daha parlak bir surette beyan ve isbat eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants without knowledge include leaders such as Nadr b. al-Harith and Abu Jahl; an earlier parallel addresses their followers who imitate them.
rows.anchor: Nadr b. Hâris ve Ebû Cehil gibi şeytanetkâr rüesâ-yı mücâdilîn hakkında yukarıda geçen nazîri de böylelerin arkasına düşen mukallidîn hakkındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their debate rests on conjecture and feelings rather than certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: Yani yakīnî bir ilim ile değil, mücerred zann u hissiyâtına tebe‘an

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God “on an edge” means practicing religion from the margin for a particular aim, rather than wholeheartedly, or becoming Muslim only verbally.
rows.anchor: Yani cân ü gönülden değil de bir kenardan, bir maksad-ı mahsus için dindarlık eder veya dil ucuyla Müslüman olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a person is content when good comes but turns away when hardship tests him.
rows.anchor: da kendisine bir hayır isabet ederse ona mutmain olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion of revelation names Uyaina b. Badr, Aqra b. Habis, and Abbas b. Mirdas among those who would accept Muhammad's religion if it brought them good, otherwise call it false.
rows.anchor: müellefetü’l-kulûbdan Uyeyne b. Bedr, Akra‘b. Hâbis, Abbas b. Mirdas birbirlerine
